subject: Pilot pricing for low-volume customers — per-call minimums, context carry, and invoice smoothing
messages:
From: Carlos Ruiz <carlos.ruiz@acmehealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Health Billing <billing@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot pricing question — low monthly volume

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for running the technical pilot with our team. A few finance folks pinged me with questions before we sign the SOW — wanted to make sure we and the procurement team understand how small-volume usage will be billed so we don't get surprised on the first invoice. Quick items: 

- We expect ~2k calls/month but most calls are very small (few tens of tokens) — do you have a per-call minimum or quantum? How does rounding work?
- Some requests include long EHR context (up to ~6k tokens); do you bill the full context + output? Any examples you can share?
- KV-cache / prefix reuse: for repeated patient lookups, do cached tokens still bill?
- Billing cadence and pilot concession: if we run under the pilot SOW, can you smooth the first invoice or apply a one-off credit to avoid invoice volatility?

I attached a short sample of expected call sizes (pilot_requirements.xlsx). Please point me to any docs or give a couple of worked examples we can share with procurement.

Gracias,
Carlos
Finance Lead, Acme Health

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Ruiz <carlos.ruiz@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Acme Health Billing <billing@acmehealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot pricing question — low monthly volume

Hi Carlos — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front and I will confirm a few implementation details with our billing team (cc'd).

- Per-call minimum: We bill in "quanta". For the pilot I can propose a conservative quantum of 16 tokens (we round up to the nearest quantum per request).
- Long contexts: We bill request tokens (prompt/context uploaded) + response tokens. Long EHR contexts are billed in full unless you enable prefix/KV caching; I can show worked examples below.
- KV-cache: cache hits reduce billable prompt tokens — we treat a cache hit as 0 tokens billed for the repeated prefix. The initial warmup is billed.
- Invoice smoothing: We can offer a one-time pilot invoice smoothing credit — I need to confirm the amount with finance.

I'll loop in Karthik and Mateo to confirm the quantum and whether we can set a non-standard smoothing line item for the first month. Expect one consolidated reply from us by Monday with examples and a simple sample invoice.

Best,
Naomi
Director, Customer Finance & Pricing
Redwood Inference

Subject: ACME pilot — per-call quantum and smoothing credit (internal)

Team — forwarding Carlos's note. Key asks: per-call quantum/rounding, KV-cache accounting, and a smoothing credit for first invoice.

Notes / proposed positions: 
- Recommend using a 16-token quantum for billing math for small-volume pilots. It keeps invoices readable and aligns with our smallest compute unit.
- Billing rule: billable_tokens = ceil((prompt_tokens + response_tokens) / quantum) * quantum. For cache hits where the prefix is served from KV cache we should not bill the repeated prefix tokens (only billed on first warmup request per session/prefix).
- For long contexts (6k tokens), the same rule applies; ensure we show examples for: short call (12 tokens prompt + 8 tokens response), medium (300 + 60), long (6000 + 80).

Karthik — can you confirm the KV-cache behavior from an implementation standpoint (do we credit back warmup tokens if we see sustained reuse across same customer sessions)?
Mateo — if we offer a smoothing credit, recommend a fixed credit equal to the expected delta between raw charges and a 30-day smoothed baseline. For their volume (~2k calls) I estimate a one-time credit of ~4,000 quanta (64k tokens) is too large — suggest instead a pilot credit of 500 quanta (8k tokens) which should absorb rounding noise. Thoughts?
Tessa — we'll need to surface this credit as a line item on the first invoice. Can we create a "Pilot Smoothing Credit" line that offsets token charges?

Thanks,
Naomi

Hi Carlos — thanks for your patience. Quick consolidated response and a small pilot concession that should avoid a surprise first invoice. See attached sample invoice (example_invoice_sim.csv) and the SOW link (pilot_SOW_v1.pdf) for reference.

What we'll bill (clear, with examples):
1) Quantum and rounding: We bill in a 16-token quantum. Each request is rounded up to the nearest quantum. Example: 12 prompt + 8 response = 20 tokens -> ceil(20/16)=2 quanta -> 32 tokens billed.
2) Long contexts: We bill prompt + response. Example: 6,000 context + 80 response => 6,080 tokens -> ceil(6080/16)=380 quanta -> 6,080 tokens billed (no additional surcharge).
3) KV-cache and reuse: The first request that populates a prefix/KV cache is billed in full. Subsequent requests that are satisfied from the cache do not bill the repeated prefix tokens; only additional prompt tokens and response tokens are billed. (Implementation note: cache fullness is session-bound — we'll document how to pin prefixes if needed.)
4) Pilot smoothing credit: For the first invoice only we will apply a one-time "Pilot Smoothing Credit" of 500 quanta (equivalent to 8,000 tokens) that appears as a credit line to offset rounding noise and bootstrapping costs. This is a goodwill concession for the pilot — it does not recur.

Action items / next steps: 
- Naomi (me) will attach the sample invoice and SOW (done).
- Carlos/Billing: confirm you are OK with the 16-token quantum and the one-time 500-quanta credit.
- Tessa will coordinate that the credit is applied as a separate invoice line once finance approves (Tessa: ETA?).

If that works, we'll proceed to sign the SOW and spin up the pilot in your test region. Happy to hop on a quick 15-min call to walk procurement through the math.

Thanks,
Naomi
Director, Customer Finance & Pricing
Redwood Inference
